headline: High-risk pair: shared write-capable, networked agents can conflict and cascade errors; prompt-injection and leakage are moderate due to shared file/MCP surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose shared file/MCP-style surfaces and can ingest content from those channels. agent_a uses MCP and stdin/stdout; agent_b uses runtime-injected MCPs, hooks, and reads AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path even without a documented direct bridge. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b reads agent_a-produced files or MCP messages as instructions without provenance checks
IF either agent processes attacker-controlled repository text as executable guidance
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction parsing from shared files
Require provenance tags on MCP payloads
Separate agent workspaces
Review AGENTS.md and README.md handling rules
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches repository metadata, task prompts, and code; agent_b touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data. Both have network egress and file surfaces, so a shared workspace could leak sensitive context between them. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or home-directory workspace
IF either agent uploads file contents or session history to external services
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict each agent to a distinct workspace
Redact secrets from shared files
Turn off unnecessary network egress
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and has broad network egress. Both support multiple instances, so concurrent writes to the same repo or config can race. Because agent_a explicitly modifies git state and agent_b can alter files via browser-driven workflows, the conflict blast radius includes irreversible repo corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or config directory
IF either agent performs writes without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during the other's run
Snapshot the repo before concurrent use
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is positioned to generate analysis, route/explain/build outputs, while agent_b has team_send_message and team_task_create actions plus browser/network access. That makes it plausible for B to treat A's output as authoritative and then act on it. The pair therefore supports a default cascade from generated content to downstream actions, with potentially irreversible external effects.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without verification
IF agent_b uses team_send_message or team_task_create based on A-produced claims
mitigations: Insert a human verification step
Require citations before action execution
Limit agent_b to read-only review mode
Log and diff A outputs before use
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles provider authentication data and session history, while agent_a handles task prompts and repository metadata. Both are open-source and docs-only, but the profiles show different data classes and retention-sensitive surfaces. A compliance mismatch is plausible if the pair shares regulated data or logs across installations; the evidence is indirect, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in shared session history or logs
IF one installation retains authentication data longer than the other
mitigations: Separate retention buckets
Avoid placing regulated data in shared logs
Review auth-data handling settings
Document residency and retention boundaries
requires-engineering: align deletion/export workflows across agents
